code_identity.py.gotcha: It CANNOT be built from mtime and size - that is exactly what CPython uses to decide a .pyc is fresh, so a check from the same two inputs agrees with it by construction, collisions included. The only witness that survives one is co_firstlineno, which comes from the BYTECODE while the source is read fresh. Three instrument bugs on the way, each caught by a count: functools.wraps copies __module__ onto a wrapper whose code lives in contextlib (two unrelated modules both reported drifted at the SAME line 242), CPython points co_firstlineno at the FIRST DECORATOR so accepting any '@' line swallowed everything, and skipping COMMENT lines while walking to the def let a function that had moved 40 lines be re-found and reported clean. Decorators and blanks only. And on this Mac the cache is NOT in __pycache__ - sys.pycache_prefix puts it under ~/Library/Caches/com.apple.python.
code_identity.py.purpose: Answers whether THIS interpreter's loaded bytecode agrees with the source on disk, by comparing each function's co_firstlineno against where the file says it starts. Built after three pushes of one identical tree read green, RED, green, with the red one's traceback naming a line and a variable that do not exist in the file. Distinct from console_doctor's 'running code matches disk', which asks the CONSOLE over the wire about its own image.

code_staleness.py.gotcha: It CHANGES and BLOCKS nothing — no reload, no restart, no button. And a module that never called snapshot() answers UNKNOWN, not FRESH: 'nothing snapshotted' is not the same as current. snapshot() is a one-shot no-op on re-call by design — re-snapping would adopt today's disk as the baseline and the watchdog could never report STALE again. Its real purpose is `registry_may_be_incomplete`: it separates 'I do not know this evidence source' from 'this source may not exist', the conflation that made a 16-hour-old console accuse its own .self_arming.jsonl of forgery.
code_staleness.py.purpose: The stale-image watchdog: records each watched module's (mtime,size) at first use and answers FRESH / STALE / UNKNOWN about whether this process still runs the code on disk.

coldread.py.purpose: Stages a shipped bible.html AT THE REPO ROOT and screenshots tabs/widths/regions for the cold second-eye pass, refusing to hand over a bad frame.

confidence.py.purpose: The ONE home for Wilson lower-bound + confluence scoring — how sure we are given how many looks, and how many KINDS of evidence agreed.

conftest.py.gotcha: It is a CANARY, not a lock — it reports damage after the bytes are gone. console_doctor.py.purpose: The EAGLE EYE: one pass over the RUNNING console; each check answers OK / MISSING(action) / UNKNOWN(why), never a bare boolean.

console_healer.py.gotcha: Silent means OFF — without TV_AUTO_HEAL=1 it still scars everything and only reports what it WOULD have done. frozen_frames.py.purpose: Reads capture files for two separate states: FROZEN (repeated sha256 of bytes) and BLANK (decoded pixels judged by paint_witness).

g5_grok_eyes.py.purpose: The second eye's vision lane: `grok -p` on his SuperGrok login, off/shadow/primary, reading the same area/tz/scene/names/names_loc/sockets JSON under an hourly+daily budget.

g5_shadow_reducer.py.gotcha: READ-SIDE ONLY. It never writes the shadow log and never prefers a lane: a 67.6% disagreement rate is a finding about the INSTRUMENTS, not a vote to settle. One-sided rows (only one lane answered) are NOT disagreements and are counted separately; rows where neither answered are not evidence at all. A rate with no denominator is UNKNOWN, never 0.0.
g5_shadow_reducer.py.purpose: Reduces tv/.g5_shadow.jsonl - the 6,082 Claude-vs-Grok rows written since 2026-08-23 that nothing had ever read - into an agreement report carrying its own denominator and window.

gate_costs.py.purpose: the MEASURED CI seconds of every gate (tv/gate_costs.json), so run_gates --shard balances the CI matrix on real cost instead of declared timeout.

Refresh from CI job logs with python3 tv/gate_costs.py <logs>; test_the_gate_set_shards_cleanly refuses a table covering under 95% of the registry.

A missing or unreachable proven sha, a failed diff, or a gate whose inputs cannot be named runs the gate. A FAIL is not stored. GitHub CI does not consult it. git_quiet.py.gotcha: Git for Windows' PATH git (Git\cmd\git.exe) is a 46 KB CUI WRAPPER and pythonw owns no console, so a CUI child ALLOCATES one — a real terminal on top of D2R. MEASURED 2026-09-21: windows stealing focus 2-3 in a row every couple of minutes. CREATE_NO_WINDOW on the wrapper is NOT enough because it respawns the real git without the flag, and headless-git.exe still starts a CUI git.exe child — so this calls mingw64\bin\git.exe DIRECTLY. It is a module rather than a helper inside control_app because console_doctor spawns git too and a second copy would drift; test_windows_git_spawns_hide_the_console pins that there may only ever be ONE body of the mingw redirect.
git_quiet.py.purpose: The ONE door every git spawn in this codebase walks through, so no git child ever owns a console.

grok_chat_prune.py.gotcha: It prunes only when NEEDED (the Grok sessions folder over 2 GB, or the disk under the ON AIR floor) and never a session active_sessions.json lists as open - an unreadable registry prunes nothing. Whole conversation folders, oldest first, never one written in the last hour or younger than 7 days (1 under the critical floor), never anything outside the root or behind a link. The console calls it from the disk sign's pass, which already waits out his game and a busy machine.
grok_chat_prune.py.purpose: #151 (REG-2743, his ruling) - prunes his own Grok CLI chats automatically when they need to be, so ~/.grok/sessions cannot take the disk to ENOSPC again (11.25 GB on 2026-09-01), with a receipt per pass.

guest_fixture_pack.py.gotcha: A pack is NOT a copied reel: one reel measured 196 MB / 153 frames, a pack of it is 2.7 MB / 16, spaced EVENLY so the scrub bar still travels the whole run (a head slice leaves the reel controls untestable past the opening). ⚠ A fixture gets its OWN namespaced sessionId — keeping the source's made the loader dedupe it against the real session list and the real row won, so the fixture flag never reached the guest. load() refuses any destination under tv/frames: a pack may be BUILT from footage and never LOADED into it.
guest_fixture_pack.py.purpose: Turns one recorded reel into a versioned, checksummed regression pack the guest seat can click: a representative subset of frames, flagged as a fixture, loadable only into a mirror.

guest_profile.py.gotcha: The rewrite is a REDACTION, not a relabel. The guest seat renders a mirror of the live console and this repo is public, so scrub() walks dict KEYS as well as values — per-session dumps are KEYED by path, and a values-only walk leaks the home directory one filename at a time. The identity is REPLACED rather than merged so an unknown key cannot ride along. ⚠ leaks() and the scrub read the SAME pair list, so a detector that forgets a secret is blind to it — callers must also check literals.
guest_profile.py.purpose: The Grok actor for the guest seat plus the redaction that keeps a public mirror publishable: a stable identity, and a deep scrub of the owner's install id, hostname, user and home paths out of every payload the box will serve.

handoff.py.gotcha: ⚠ THE WATERMARK MOVES ONLY WITH --mark, NEVER BY DRAINING - so reading the queue can never mark an unanswered ACT as read. Measured 2026-09-18: #180 held 1,177 comments / 2.55 MB and was taking 140 comments a day against 10 replies; the watermark drain is 65.5x cheaper. It still drains the CLOSED queues 179/180 on purpose, because the GrokBot native seat kept posting there after the rotation to #230.
handoff.py.purpose: Drains the GrokBot/Grok handoff queues in O(new) rather than O(all), using a stored watermark plus the REST `since` parameter, and sorts each comment into ACT / ASK / FYI so a brief cannot be lost in a wall of watch ticks.

health_engine.py.gotcha: IT REPORTS AND NEVER REPAIRS (a test pins that nothing here writes, deletes or restarts) — and it is not an AUTHORITY either: frame_authority owns deletion, chronicle_retro owns grounding, this only reports on them. UNKNOWN is a first-class state and never renders as ok; a check that raises becomes UNKNOWN, not a failure.
health_engine.py.purpose: The console's one red/green flag engine: nine checks (lanes, armed_migration, board_join, orphans, shelf witnesses, shadow_watch, readers_agree, self_arming, lane_liveness) each returning ok/warn/blocked/unknown.

heart.py.gotcha: The FLOWING branch is documented as UNREACHABLE with real data: `scored` is keyed on the ORGAN rows' ids (lanes, readers, selfArming, board_join) while `watcher` is a LANE name (tvd-eagle-watch and siblings) — two disjoint vocabularies, so `scored.get(watcher)` is always None. So a 'WATCHED, go sabotage it' prompt names work that cannot land. Also: it NEVER writes or caches (a gate asserts the module opens no file), counts are derived not typed, DARK != UNKNOWN, and WATCHED is work owed, not a fault.
heart.py.purpose: Derives every self-running vessel into ONE vocabulary — FLOWING / WATCHED / DARK / UNKNOWN — from lane_census, health rows and the lock ledger.

heart2.py.gotcha: v1 asks whether the SYSTEM is healthy; v2 asks whether the INSTRUMENTS can still go red — measured 2026-09-08, the heart was green while 12 of 238 gates were red and 8 were blind. Tampering happens ONLY in a safe_copy.py sandbox (never cp -R: tv/ is 5,865 MB of footage and a full copy once caused ENOSPC), and it PROPOSES into .heart2_proposals.md — it never edits a guard. A gate that fails its CLEAN run is UNPROVABLE, not BLIND; a sabotage whose `find` matches ≠ `matches` is the usual culprit, so the match count is printed. It is a RATCHET (the unproven backlog may only shrink), not a ban.
heart2.py.purpose: HEART 2.0 — the census of the gates themselves: re-tampers every guard that declares a RED_PROOF in a sandbox to prove it can still go red, and classifies each as proven / blind / unproven / unprovable.

heart2_candidates.py.gotcha: It refuses far more often than it proposes — anchor shorter than 8 chars, zero matches, more than one match, or an unresolvable target file all abort with a named reason. It returns TEXT only: it never writes to a guard and never writes to a target file.
heart2_candidates.py.purpose: Derives a ready-to-run red-proof (sabotage) candidate from a gate's own assertIn literals, so the proposal is actionable instead of a name.

heart_map.py.gotcha: `--check` REFUSES and never regenerates, exactly like blueprint.py, because the pre-push grades the WORKING TREE. ⚠ And an unreadable input is a REFUSAL, never a zero: `_read` returns None (v3231 — it used to return "", so an unreadable control_ui.html gave an empty id set and would have BANKED a HEART.md claiming the console paints 0 surfaces). A watcher that cannot be read is named rather than skipped, because dropping it makes every surface it covers look UNWATCHED — a coverage collapse indistinguishable from a real one. `_why_unmeasurable` is TOLD what the caller found and must never re-read the file: bump_version replaces the surfaces atomically and regenerates this map in the same run, so a second look can see a healthy file and strip the reason out of the refusal (v3235).
heart_map.py.purpose: Derives HEART.md from the tree: every `id` the console and the board PAINT, and which of them a watcher's CODE names whole. heart_floor.json is a ratchet by NAME. A regeneration raises it whenever the map still watches every floor name. --check refuses a fall, a lost name, or a floor that lags the map. Only `--bless --why` lowers it. Both files are written whole after their text is built (REG-3216).

his_answers.py.gotcha: A changed fingerprint REOPENS the question and keeps the old answer as stale history; ruled holds 30 days, snooze 7, handoff until the question changes. An unreadable store is reported and NEVER written over. The path is chosen by the console (_decision_path), so each machine keeps its own answers.
his_answers.py.purpose: Keeps his answers to the questions THIS console asked him (console_doctor.ASKS), one per question with the question's fingerprint, and applies them at read time so an answered question stops billing him and the row says what he chose.

hover_calibration.py.gotcha: It drives NOTHING — hover_mode moves the pointer and this is a passive witness of it, and record_step swallows its own errors so it can never strand his cursor. With no steps recorded calibrate() returns None and says why rather than emitting a plausible constant, which would place every item in the wrong cell with total confidence.
hover_calibration.py.purpose: Records mini auto's (planned frame target, screen point) pairs while it hovers and derives the tooltip->cell offset slot_identity refuses without.

hover_drive.py.gotcha: There is NO click by CONSTRUCTION, not by setting — no mouse-down/up event is ever built, so no flag or future caller can make it press (a left click on an occupied D2R cell picks the item up). It aborts the moment the pointer drifts more than 6px from where it left it, because his hand on the mouse wins, and it converts each target through screen_point() one at a time so a dragged window cannot leave a stale batch of coordinates.
hover_drive.py.purpose: The only file that moves his pointer: hovers slot_identity targets to reveal tooltips, building kCGEventMouseMoved and nothing else.

hover_mode.py.gotcha: It exists because both ends already existed and nothing joined them — `hover_drive.walk()` had ZERO callers, so the button he was looking for did not render. Four stop conditions, three of them his: if HIS HAND touches the mouse the sweep aborts and the pointer is deliberately NOT restored (fighting him for it is worse than leaving it). `status()` returning running:False with stopped:None means it has NEVER RUN — a different fact from 'ran and finished', and the UI must distinguish them. start() refuses a second concurrent sweep.
hover_mode.py.purpose: Joins the hover PLAN to the pointer ACTUATOR: sweeps each occupied stash cell so the game renders its tooltip. It moves only — it never clicks.

hover_wilson.py.gotcha: THE DENOMINATOR IS SABOTAGE ATTEMPTS, NOT RUNS — an always-agreeing check may be perfect or INERT (vault_autoreel_tick ran every 45s for months at 100% agreement having swept nothing), so a claim nobody tried to break scores UNPROVEN, and UNPROVEN must not read as failing. It runs on synthetic RECTANGLES, not his screen: no cursor moves, no window opens, safe in CI and safe while he plays. It is a REPORT not a gate — run_gates invokes it with -c and it has no failing mode, so it always exits 0. bank_into_proof_queue folds by (lock, kind, src) so re-running REPLACES rather than inflating n; attempts=None banks NOTHING.
hover_wilson.py.purpose: Scores the MINI/hover autopilot's four independently-failing claims — COORDINATE, ANCHOR, READ, SLOT — with a Wilson lower bound and banks them into the self-arming lock ledger.

human_eyes_gate.py.gotcha: Nothing imports it — run_gates.py:4345 registers it as Gate('human-eyes', ... '--gate'). It does NOT perform the A13 contradiction check (a LOOKED observation vs the live console) because a gate has no running console; it asserts only proven/owed/readable. For its whole early life it was registered as `--prove` ONLY, so it sabotaged fixtures and never opened his real ledger. Exit 77 = declared SKIP (no ledger on this venue), which is not a pass.
human_eyes_gate.py.purpose: Gate over the human-eyes LOOKED ledger: proves the loop ran end to end and no brief is OWED past its patience. 77 = declared skip.

human_eyes_ledger.py.gotcha: All three of its file-IO handlers return None, never [] — swallow_census cites this file as the purest instance of the honest shape, because None lets a caller tell 'could not ask' from 'no briefs'; flipping them to [] is the RANK-1 defect the ratchet exists to stop. It stores `saw` (raw observation) separately from `conclusion` on purpose: a brief that returns a conclusion with no observation reads like evidence and is not — a Grok pass quoted PROJECT_VAULT_MANAGER.md accurately and reported the wrong gate numbers. The ledger (.human_eyes.jsonl, overridable via TV_HUMAN_EYES_LEDGER) is a runtime record and is gitignored.
human_eyes_ledger.py.purpose: Records the Grok-Bot human-eyes loop: which briefs were SENT, which came back with a raw OBSERVATION plus verdict, and which are still owed.

inventory_law.py.gotcha: Deliberately NOT a roster — it word-boundary-matches the words D2R itself prints, because a reader hands over OCR of a tooltip, not a database id. LOCKED is tested BEFORE consumable and the order is load-bearing: a *Scroll* of Town Portal is a consumable while the TOME is furniture, and a reader that saw both on one line must not get the tome demoted. It changes no behaviour — it exists to give the retro readers the answer control_app already had.
inventory_law.py.purpose: The hardcoded three-class item law — LOCKED furniture (Horadric Cube, tomes, Wirt's Leg, keys), CONSUMABLE (potions, scrolls, gold), and LOOT, the only class worth a register.

item_identity.py.gotcha: Two vocabularies for one item, on one axis: a QUALIFIER (Latent/Renewed) is IDENTITY and never folds; an apostrophe byte, a base-type tail and an unambiguous parenthetical are RENDERING and do. ⚠ The parenthetical is decided by MEASUREMENT, not punctuation — 'Athena's Wrath' is a unique and nothing else so '(set piece)' folds, while 'Crescent Moon' is a unique AND a runeword so '(amulet)' is the only thing separating two real items.
item_identity.py.purpose: The two vocabularies for one item: what the VAULT calls a physical thing and what the CHRONICLE calls a grail line, separating identity from rendering so a Latent charm never witnesses a renewed one and an apostrophe byte never splits a row in two.

item_tables.py.gotcha: THE STATS BLOCK AND AN ITEM USE DIFFERENT WIDTHS for the same stat: csvBits (character 'gf' section) vs saveBits (item bitstream) - strength is 10 bits in one and 8 in the other, and reading one with the other derails. A table KEY is not a display name: 97 unique keys differ from what the game prints (Thudergod's Vigor is Thundergod's Vigor), so names come from item-names.json / item-runes.json and `namesFrom` says which. runes.txt has no Runeword80, so the row and the RunewordN key disagree from row 80 on; both are stored and neither is picked. Never wrap the pull in the perl alarm idiom (see affix_lexicon).
item_tables.py.purpose: Generates tv/item_tables.json from the D2R CASC: exactly what tv/d2s_read.py needs to decode a character save - per stat id its item and character-save bit widths, per item code its display name, kind (armor/weapon/misc) and stackable flag, uniques and set items by *ID, and runewords by 1-based runes.txt row. load() returns None, never an empty dict, when it has not been generated.

journal_drain.py.gotcha: It refuses far more often than it writes, and every refusal is deliberate. It will not run without an explicit yes, will not run if a backup did not verify row-for-row, will not run if the corpus moved since the plan judged it, and will not rename its rewrite over a file whose INODE changed — tv_diablo rotates the ring with os.replace, which makes sessions.1.jsonl GROW, so a line count cannot see it. Identity comes from os.fstat of the handle it read, never from the path.
journal_drain.py.purpose: The WRITER half of the journal drain: it backs up every generation of the session journal, removes the rows a plan released, and carries forward anything the recorder appended while it was writing. It exists as its own module because test_a_journal_row_leaves_only_on_proof forbids the PLANNER from holding any write-capable call, so the planner decides and this acts.

journal_retention.py.gotcha: Name suggests the reel river; it is the OTHER half. The reel side is finished (20 reels, ROUTED 20, TOMBSTONE 0 — correct, all three refusal groups are legitimate) while his shelf still shows 419 journal rows, ~195 of which name film that no longer exists. 'No film at all' is HELD, not extracted — absence of film is not proof of extraction. And it DELETES NOTHING; the apply half is his decision. Four rows are never releasable: newest 8, film still on disk, reels the test suite opens by name, and undatable rows.
journal_retention.py.purpose: Classifies shelf JOURNAL rows as RELEASABLE (footageState == retired) or HELD, keeps the newest 8, and explains every hold. Writes nothing.

js_syntax_gate.py.gotcha: A hand-rolled tokenizer was tried and REJECTED — it reported 14-16 false problems on files that parse perfectly, because these pages use template literals with nested backticks, embedded HTML and regex literals a heuristic cannot tell from division. So it asks a real engine. And when no browser is available it SKIPS LOUDLY: a gate that cannot run must say so, never pass silently.
js_syntax_gate.py.purpose: Loads bible.html and tv/control_ui.html in a real JS engine (Chromium via CDP, or node) and fails on any SyntaxError — one bad escape or mid-line comment blanks the whole 37k-line page.

keep_awake.py.gotcha: The Windows execution state is PER THREAD and the OS drops it when that thread ends, so a pid hold lives on its own watcher thread (take, WaitForSingleObject on the process handle, release with ES_CONTINUOUS alone - all on that thread); a release from any other thread releases nothing. The flags are exactly 0x80000001 - never ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED (his screen still turns off), never away mode, never powercfg or the registry. macOS is `caffeinate -i -w <pid>`, spawned with an absolute executable and close_fds=False because the console has Quartz loaded (#150's fork deadlock). A lid close still sleeps the PC: that stays the OS's call. self_prove holds a pid for real only when its OWN doors (spawn, pid_alive, proc_birth, identity - captured at import) started or verified it: a law that stubs any of them hands a stand-in pid, and a real caffeinate on that number holds whatever process owns it (the first cut started three a run from the REG-1628 chain law, one outliving the law).
keep_awake.py.purpose: #170 (REG-2483): keeps this PC awake ONLY while a proof or sweep runs - held(why) for a with-block on this thread, hold_for_pid(pid, why) for a process (idempotent, ends by itself when the pid ends, normally or killed), status() in the shared vocabulary {on, holds, lastTs, why}. self_prove takes a hold for the prover it spawns and for one a relaunched console adopts.

lane_census.py.gotcha: NOT every thread is a lane — a one-shot worker is a TASK and registering it would promise persistence it does not have, so 'started but not registered' is not automatically 'unwatched'. It carries its own `--prove` because an earlier ad-hoc version misclassified five `while True` `_loop` functions as one-shot and that answer was quoted into a GitHub issue.
lane_census.py.purpose: Classifies every threading.Thread target in control_app.py as LOOP / one-shot / UNKNOWN, and diffs that census against BLUEPRINT.md's LANES section.

lane_health.py.gotcha: The stall thresholds are an explicitly LABELLED judgement, tuned against nothing. It decides nothing and writes nothing, and an unreadable store answers UNKNOWN rather than healthy — it exists because a watchdog that spoke only on message-change made five days of silence read as fine.
lane_health.py.purpose: Per extraction lane: freshness (when it last produced work), reach (corpus covered), and divergence (two lanes disagreeing about the same session).

lane_liveness.py.gotcha: _TICKS is PROCESS memory — a cold import outside control_app reports all 20 vessels UNKNOWN, which is a fact about the reader, not the lanes; use stamping_functions(), which parses the SOURCE and answers from anywhere. The period travels WITH the stamp (a global threshold spans 0.5s to 900s, 1800x), and every_s vs dead_after_s are two different questions — padding every_s makes the report print a period the lane does not have. Ages are monotonic so a sleeping Mac is not eight hours of silence.
lane_liveness.py.purpose: THREAD-ALIVE for console loops: each loop ticks with its OWN period; rows grade FLOWING/LATE/UNTIMED/UNKNOWN/DORMANT.

lane_lock.py.gotcha: lane_for() returns None rather than picking when a frame looks like BOTH a stash and a chronicle page — that is the deliberate behaviour, not a failure to decide, because the two wrong answers are not symmetrical (a Chronicle row filed as ownership claims he owns something he only saw listed). A cheap pixel gate is NOT sufficient: measured 2026-08-18, `classify_stash_grid` calls a real Chronicle page 'stash' with frac_dark 0.5364 and 11 dark columns, and only the AI classifier gets it right. The v1999 scar: `personal` and `shared` — the two tabs he is in most — were missing from the tab tuple, so ambiguous frames were not seen as ambiguous and the lock stayed OPEN.
lane_lock.py.purpose: One key from one frame: at most ONE write lane is ever unlocked — the vault surface OR exactly one chronicle ledger — and ambiguity locks both.

lane_ports.py.gotcha: It never binds a socket and never deletes a file. A forbidden or out-of-range base is refused and current_base returns None, so adopt keeps the suite historical port. keep=True preserves a port the caller already set only when no lane base is present; a set TV_LANE_PORT_BASE overwrites it. stamp also sets TV_LAW_PORT to base plus 2 so two lanes do not share a Chrome port. His console port is in the forbidden set and is never derived.
lane_ports.py.purpose: Gives each heart2 prove lane its own port base so two sandboxes do not share 17971 or 17972, which is how one sandbox request deletes a tracked file in the other.

lane_trace.py.gotcha: A TICK IS NOT A SECOND WITNESS — lane_liveness._TICKS is an in-process dict on a monotonic clock and reads EMPTY from another process. A bare heartbeat would be an ECHO of the watchdog, so this must carry the RESULT: a loop running and producing nothing then reads as a CONTRADICTION, which is the only thing this organ can see. Writes are atomic (tmp + os.replace) because a plain open(p,'w') truncates first and an empty file reads as 'the loop produced nothing'. With min_gap_s the TRACE period is the GAP, not the tick period, and loop_corroborate.LOOPS must declare the gap or a correctly-throttled loop reads stale. note() swallows everything and returns False.
lane_trace.py.purpose: Writes one small per-lane file recording WHAT A LOOP DECIDED (drift verdict, orphan count, shadow result) so an outside process can date the loop — the second, independent witness a corroborator needs.

launcher_decide.py.gotcha: Never binds or kills anything: it only ASKS the console on the given port (/api/window, /api/freshness, /api/status moduleFreshness) and POSTs a front request. Exit 0 = the console came forward, the launcher ends; exit 3 = replace it (it SAYS it is older than the disk or has no window, or nothing serves the port); exit 2 = could not tell (a timeout, an ok:false or unreadable answer, a window mode it does not know, the 9 s budget ran out) - the console is left running. REG-1940: exit 1 is never a verdict, because an uncaught exception exits 1; the Windows launcher read 1 as consent and Stop-Process -Forced a fullscreen or slow console.
launcher_decide.py.purpose: REG-1514/1758/1940 - both launchers' one decision: bring the running console forward, leave it running, or let the launcher replace it (v1379.1's stale-code case and a windowless console only).

launcher_pull.py.gotcha: Classifies against the origin/main already fetched, then resets only when a second read still says every tracked change is a plain modification whose bytes match that blob (CR ignored), HEAD is an ancestor of it, and no untracked path would be replaced. git reset --hard replaces such a file and exits 0. The added-path list uses -z and --no-renames: without -z the names arrive as one string, so an untracked file among them is missed and the reset replaces it, and without --no-renames a similar rename is hidden. A file that occupies a path the update turns into a directory is in the way only when that file is not tracked; a tracked file is the update and the reset must land. A tracked directory that holds an untracked file is in the way, because the reset deletes that directory. An ignored file inside that directory is in the way too. Names are asked as literal paths, so a bracket is not a wildcard. A symlink is not treated as a directory, so an untracked link in that place stays. A name that is not UTF-8 stops the reset. A real edit, a file in the way, a history that is not a fast-forward, or a git that cannot be read resets nothing. It does not fetch. Fetching first would make the on-disk update no longer match origin, and the pull would stay blocked.
launcher_pull.py.purpose: The launcher pull decision: a file that matches the fetched update is that update, not a local edit.

law_widths.py.gotcha: A PROVING DEVICE, NEVER A VERDICT: run_gates.run() calls scrub() before its first gate and heart2's _run_gate drops TV_LAW_WIDTHS from every run it did not restrict itself, so the full width sweep stays the verdict of record (CI never sets it). Unset or empty means EVERY width; garbage refuses rather than silently narrowing.
law_widths.py.purpose: The one reader of TV_LAW_WIDTHS (#42): at push time heart2 --prove --push hands a width-law red-proof the viewports its defect was MEASURED to show at, and the width laws restrict every width loop to that set.

ledger3.py.gotcha: It opens NO file and names NO store: control_app._ledger3_stores hands it the loaded objects (journal ring, chronicle book, vault ledger, shelf path, river stamps, survey, tombstones), each resolved through that module's own path authority, so a fixture never reaches his tree and a law drives the whole record over temp stores. Every key is borrowed, never copied: chronicle_retro._reel_key (one reel, two spellings), item_identity.vault_key + trace_spine.name_key (one name), vault_retro.look_id folded by _fold_bare_sessions (one VISIT per trial, never a frame - his §34.2 ruling), vault_evidence.tier (the one table), chronicle_retro.witnesses (the one independence verdict). A provisional OCR-only name is listed apart and never counted as named (measured: 'Your Gamlng Rlg Is Readyl' x4 rides his journal as names). An unreadable side is None with a sentence in `unknown`, never 0; a session no store knows is ok:False. The reader-vs-vault agreement is two engines shown side by side and never averaged. An unkeyable gate is never run alongside (never banked), so the final push still runs it. After the import it says FULL or PARTIAL (REG-2594): every assigned proof CI banked nothing for and this Mac does not prove alongside is owed; a PARTIAL set exits 3 and never runs --final.
proof_keys_mac.py.purpose: REG-2590 - the Mac driver: push HEAD to ci/proof-keys-<sha12>, prove alongside only the gates CI cannot bank, wait for this commit's fan-in, download its set and `heart2 --import-shards` it.

vault_page_node.py.purpose: V1c (#152 item 4): the WHOLE bible.html in node - every inline <script> in page order in one global world over a small DOM/localStorage stand-in (ids from the markup and from every innerHTML it writes), storage starting EMPTY, timers queued until the body flushes them, and no network at all (fetch, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon inert). run(body) boots the page, fires DOMContentLoaded and load, runs the body and returns the OUT it filled; PATCHES are exact find/replace pairs applied to the source first (a law counts calls with them), a PRELUDE runs before the first page script, and clock/seed make two runs comparable byte for byte. The vault laws that must see a hand add as it ships (test_a_hand_add_is_not_quadratic, test_the_vault_memo_changes_no_answer) and the speed bench stand on it.
vault_page_node.py.gotcha: It is not a browser: querySelectorAll answers [], layout is zero, and innerHTML costs nothing, so it measures the page's JavaScript and never its DOM (a Chrome-only cost needs a Playwright spec on CI). A PATCH whose anchor matches the wrong number of times fails the run by name (PATCH ANCHOR MOVED), never silently. The page's console goes to stderr and OUT travels on one marked stdout line, because a page log after the body would otherwise be read as the answer. A script that throws at boot is listed in OUT.__boot.errors - a law must assert that list is empty, or it is measuring half a page.

vault_speed_bench.py.purpose: V1c (#152 item 4): the hand-add speed CURVE - N hand adds (default 50/200/550) on a fresh whole page in node through the real door (vaultHandAdd) and through his click (vaultHandTake, which repaints after every add), printing per size the total, the mean of the last 10 adds before each mark and one paint. --memo-off sets window._vaultMemoOff = true, which is the path v3784 took, so before and after are measured on one tree.
vault_speed_bench.py.gotcha: A REPORT, not a gate: a clock moves with the load on the box, so the gate is test_a_hand_add_is_not_quadratic (it counts work). 550 adds with the memos off take 10-20 minutes in node, and node is not Chrome - GrokBot's perf3.py on his screen is the browser measurement.

ls_wal_guard.py.gotcha: It never truncates a WAL while any process holds it: TRUNCATE holds the writer lock while waiting on WebKit's readers and a WebKit write that hits busy is a lost localStorage write, so the live 30-min look is PASSIVE only and the shrink happens at the next --open startup. Holders that lsof cannot read are UNKNOWN and skipped. A holder found at startup is a leftover from an earlier console (no WebView exists yet) and is reported, never killed.
ls_wal_guard.py.purpose: Automatic pruning of the Mac native console's WebKit LocalStorage write-ahead log (localstorage.sqlite3-wal, which reached 26 GB): wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) + integrity_check at startup before the WebView, and a 30-minute size watch that publishes lsWal on /api/status.

d2jsp_price_db.py.gotcha: An outlier (w 0) stays on record but never moves the price. fresh_refresh pauses while a gate or heart2 run holds the tree, so a refresh during checks says paused rather than reading.
d2jsp_price_db.py.purpose: The d2jsp price DB: every priced post the desk read, keyed once by its forum link, priced by an age-decayed weighted median with a Wilson confidence and a separate perfect tier.

launcher_icon.py.gotcha: Only the icon resource is replaced and the bundle touched; a bundle is never moved, renamed or deleted, and one that runs another tree is left alone.
launcher_icon.py.purpose: On each launch, gives every TV DIABLO.app on the Desktop or in Applications that runs this repo's start_tvd_mac.sh the repo's current appicon.icns.

farmed_names.py.gotcha: A word that matches nothing is dropped, never shown; UI and NPC words come from bible.html _NOT_ITEMS plus SESSION_UI_WORDS; potions and other consumables are never farmed, uber keys and organs are.
farmed_names.py.purpose: Snaps OCR words from a session to known D2 item names (item_tables.json) and groups what a run farmed, with counts.

fleet_presence.py.gotcha: Being in the site's online list is not enough: the presence key outlives a sleeping PC by its TTL.
fleet_presence.py.purpose: The one ONLINE/offline rule every Fleet surface asks: a fresh beacon or a live recorder is online, anything else says how long ago it was seen.

recorder_lease.py.gotcha: A lease whose pid is dead is free; two recorders at once once killed dwm.exe, so a claim never runs beside a live holder.
recorder_lease.py.purpose: One lease file lets the recorder and the reel-cutter outlive their console, and lets a restarted console adopt them instead of starting a second.

session_route.py.gotcha: A floor-only sighting is seen, never farmed; an item read from a trade, vendor, gamble or shared-stash screen is carried, never farmed. Identify renames a farmed item without counting it again. A chronicle find needs the green 'eligible for chronicle' line.
session_route.py.purpose: v3859 (#230) - the session route ledger: walks one session's reads and files every item as farmed, identified, stashed, trashed, carried or seen, the one route the owner Sessions tab and every shadow read.

read_identity.py.gotcha: A conflict between signals is kept side by side and the attribution is UNKNOWN, never a guess; the game password is cut before the password word and never leaves this module.
read_identity.py.purpose: One extractor of a read's identity signals (game name and farming series, the login character, the character panel, the avatar class) that sessions, the River, the Vault evidence and the Fleet consume.

ci_speed.py.gotcha: GitHub's own job records only (created -> started is the queue, started -> completed the job, first created -> last completed the wall); a job never started or finished is counted unfinished, never timed. The ledger is machine-wide (git's common dir). observe() never raises: a round that cannot be measured is said, and the ship goes on.
ci_speed.py.purpose: #194 - whether the rounds keep getting faster: every round's workflows measured when GitHub vouches and said against their earlier rounds; `python3 tv/ci_speed.py --show` prints the ledger.

ci_verdict.py.gotcha: UNKNOWN (gh unreachable) is never green, and a dirty tree is never asked about - the pre-push grades the working tree. The shard caches are HIDDEN files (.heart2_cache.json): `*.json` never matches them (REG-3154).
ci_verdict.py.purpose: Does GitHub vouch for this exact commit? GREEN when every REQUIRED workflow's newest run on the sha succeeded, or (REG-3652) when that run's required jobs (Linux seed, ci shards, fan-in) have all succeeded even if non-required proof-keys windows jobs are still running. The pre-push's ci-trust asks it, and --mac-only names the changed laws only this Mac can prove.

proof_release.py.gotcha: The unpack takes ONLY proof-shard-<k>/.heart2_cache.json regular files and refuses the whole bundle on anything else; TLS is never unverified (a forged bundle would mark laws proven). absent/unknown are asked again, never 'imported'.
proof_release.py.purpose: Each console imports GitHub's proofs for its own commit from the public proof-bank release (proofs-<sha>[-win32].tgz) into heart2 --import-shards, so no PC re-proves what GitHub proved.

ship_when_green.py.gotcha: Refuses a dirty tree and a non-fast-forward; stops on the first red run and names it; never --no-verify, never a forced main.
ship_when_green.py.purpose: The ship: the exact commit to ci/claude-vNNNN + ci/proof-keys-vNNNN, any path-filtered REQUIRED workflow dispatched, GitHub's verdict polled, main pushed through the hook only on GREEN REG-3653 yields dry/ and grok/ runners before the ci/ push.

repair_book.py.gotcha: It never runs anything for a miss, a row-tied entry runs only on MISSING, and a failed repair waits an hour - no install loops.
repair_book.py.purpose: The repair book: every environment fault already fixed by hand (Pillow, numpy, node, websocket-client, a shallow clone) is fixed again automatically by the console's EXISTING door, on a cadence; an unknown eagle MISSING row is a listed miss.

repair_diagnose.py.gotcha: Read-only (--allowedTools Read,Grep), run OUTSIDE the project with --add-dir (REG-3235: inside it, CLAUDE.md and paging Reads spent all 8 turns), at most 2 a day, only new misses, a failed ask keeps its reason, never under D2R_NO_CLAUDE or while he plays or a push grades - a re-read loop once maxed his weekly plan.
repair_diagnose.py.purpose: The PC's own Claude diagnoses a repair-book miss (CAUSE / FIX / VERIFY) and proposes; the proposal rides the presence row to the overwatch line.

lane_cpu.py.gotcha: Per-thread CPU from the OS with no dependency (Mach thread_info on macOS - its thread_id IS threading's native_id; GetThreadTimes on Windows; /proc on Linux). Every Mach port reference is deallocated (a port COUNT never moves on a leak - only send references do). UNKNOWN is never a zero.
lane_cpu.py.purpose: Which lane is eating the CPU: each named thread's CPU over about a minute, on /api/status (laneCpu) and the heart's busiest-lanes section (REG-3236).

fleet_errors.py.gotcha: A console that cannot be asked prints nothing (never a false all-clear); a fault that clears and returns is new again, and a proposal arriving for a shown fault is news.
fleet_errors.py.purpose: The overwatch line: each PC's unknown faults and failed repairs from the local /api/fleet, printed once per (PC, fault) for a UserPromptSubmit hook.

console_port.py.gotcha: A value of TV_CONTROL_PORT that will not read names NO console (None), never his :17772; his console is the default only when nothing in the environment names one. DELIBERATE lists the files that name his ports on purpose - test_a_scratch_console_never_addresses_his fails on a his-port number anywhere else in tv/*.py.
console_port.py.purpose: REG-2998 - the one helper through which a process addresses its OWN console (TV_CONTROL_PORT), so a scratch console a law spawns never reads or drives his live console or agent port by name.

render_bless.py.gotcha: A floor rises only to min(CI's count, this machine's push-gate count), and only where the push gate's own last FULL clean run measured above it (tv/.render_verdict.json coverageStale); a partial verdict or an incomplete CI record is refused whole, a LIVE population (render_check.COVERAGE_VOLATILE) is never raised, and nothing is ever lowered. It needs no browser - it reads the record CI's render-bless job uploaded.
render_bless.py.purpose: REG-3081/3083 (#2) - reads the coverage bless CI's render-bless workflow made on a full cold run and applies the floors that may rise on this machine, without running a browser here.

ci_watch.py.gotcha: An unread GitHub is UNKNOWN, never green, and 'slow' is RED although the run ended: his 75-minute max was passed. Scheduled routines are left out of a commit's runs. GitHub's unauthenticated API allows 60 reads an hour, so a long watch reads through gh_get (the authenticated gh CLI) and falls back to the public API; a TV_STUB test console never asks.
ci_watch.py.purpose: REG-3213 - judges one commit's GitHub Actions runs (overrun/slow/red/running/green/none/unknown) with on/worked/lastTs/owed and the jobs still running past 75 min. Asked by ship_when_green (authenticated through gh_get) and by the console's CI tick (public API, at most every 5 min).

proof_seed.py.gotcha: A seed is an optimisation: the CLI exits 0 always, and a seed that cannot be built is a cold run, said and never red. What the seed holds never decides what is served - heart2 serves a seed entry only under the key THIS checkout's bytes give it, and reads served.json only when its sha is the checkout's HEAD. Every shard checks the seed's sha256 against the seed job's digest and refuses to start on another.
proof_seed.py.purpose: REG-3210/3214 - builds a CI proof run's one seed: the restored actions/cache seed plus the proof-bank bundle of the exact head sha (and, for Windows, the newest other set), served.json and its digest. It marks a set its bound cut as bank=partial. --widen merges a re-run shard's earlier attempt into the seed; --wait-sibling waits for this commit's ci round. Never fails a run.

art_names.py.gotcha: Read-only: it opens the two pages and the HD manifest and lists art/. A composed name ('art/' + slug) is a DOOR read from the table that feeds it, and a composer it does not know is reported as an unknown door, never skipped. The board's relative art/ resolves to /art/ because the console iframes it from /board, so bible.html's names count too. A name inside a comment is not a request.
art_names.py.purpose: Every art name the console and its board can ask /art/ for, read from the code that asks (literals, 12 composers expanded from their tables, the HD manifest; an unknown composer is reported); the CLI checks an art tree and lists what will 404

disk_growers.py.gotcha: The registry is DECLARED (GROWERS): a directory no entry names is never looked at. A new entry starts in dry-run and arms itself only after ARM_AFTER_PASSES clean passes spanning ARM_AFTER_H hours. Nothing is pruned when holders cannot be read (lsof; psutil on Windows - without it a Windows PC prunes nothing and says why), and the CLI only measures - it never salvages or prunes. Age is the newest of mtime AND ctime, so a copy that kept old mtimes is young.
disk_growers.py.purpose: REG-3208/3209: the growers lane. A DECLARED registry of what keeps growing (seat worktrees and scratch in the temp root, law fixtures in $TMPDIR, %TEMP% on Windows) is measured each pass. What is informational is salvaged into tv/.salvage: unmerged commits as patches, merge history as a bundle, the dirty diff, untracked files, or one record line for a law fixture. Salvages stay under caps and a free-space floor and are read back by sha256. Only then is the grower pruned (git worktree remove for a worktree), with lsof asked again before each prune. New entries stay in dry-run until they earn arming.

silospen_places.py.gotcha: Read-only GETs to silospen's calculator, paced. A target the page already runs (andariel, countess ...) keeps the page's stored figure; only a target with no run becomes a new place, and each carries its OWN /players factor (a super-unique's treasure class is its own - Coldcrow never moves, Blood Raven x1.46). The Cow King is shown, never ranked (his kill bars that character from the cow level); random packs are priced per kill only. Never hand-edit the page's QW_* block: re-pull and --emit.
silospen_places.py.purpose: #85 - every place an early unique drops, as silospen ranks it: the bosses and super-unique Quick wins ranks by runs (QW_TARGETS / QW_PLACES / PLACE_PF in bible.html) and the checkpoints its law reads (tv/data/silospen_places_rotw30.json).

silospen_set_mf.py.gotcha: Read-only GETs to silospen's calculator (the SET rows of 8 sample items at MF 0/300/700/1000). --emit FITS each farm's monster level and quality bonus to those checkpoints and refuses a farm it cannot fit within FIT_TOL (named, never guessed); farms it does not model (the Cows, the Pit, Diablo Clone) are SKIPPED_FARMS and their sets keep the unique curve. Never hand-edit the page's SET_MF block: re-pull and --emit.
silospen_set_mf.py.purpose: #43 - a set item's odds follow the game's unique-first quality roll: writes SET_MF_FARM (farm -> [monster level, bonus]) and SET_MF_BASE (set item -> [base level, class row]) into bible.html's SET_MF block, and the checkpoints its law reads (tv/data/silospen_set_mf_rotw30.json).

silospen_tz_levels.py.gotcha: Read-only GETs to silospen's calculator, paced (monsterProbabilities, Terror Zone ON). The level search is a bisection over 1-99 - a change that reverts inside an interval would be missed (a terror zone's monster level only rises with the character's). Breakpoints are kept only when odds move past TOL (2%); the page table holds only items whose odds move.
silospen_tz_levels.py.purpose: v3884 (REG-3437, his 'Add a level setting') - silospen's terror-zone odds at every character level 1-99 for the eight boss / super-unique farms; --build writes the page's tz-level-odds table (the LVL slider reads it through the BOSSES getters), --check holds the stored TZ columns to silospen at their stored levels.

flake_ledger.py.gotcha: A known flake or infra kill may be auto-rerun once; a flake that stays green for nClean=3 is pruned. should_rerun never invents a flake from a single red.
flake_ledger.py.purpose: REG-3644 - the ship pipeline's flake ledger: which failed CI jobs may be rerun alone, and which must stop the ship.

preship.py.gotcha: Box rehearsal reports an owed second-eye and does not refuse; Mac readiness refuses it. The only safe auto-fix is a symlink to ~/d2r_bible_tests/node_modules. A missing playwright is a readiness failure, not a skip.
preship.py.purpose: REG-3642/3646 - the ship pipeline's local gates: box rehearsal of every non-Mac gate plus agreement laws, Mac worktree readiness, and the Mac hook rehearsal that runs beside the CI wait.

shard_timings.py.gotcha: Unpriced proofs are filled with the median; already-priced rows are never lowered. coverage() must stay complete or the shard-balance law fails.
shard_timings.py.purpose: REG-3643 - per-proof seconds for shard balancing, filled from the last green proof-keys rounds.

ship.py.gotcha: A thin orchestrator: ship() in ship_when_green.py defaults the new stages OFF so existing unit tests stay isolated; this entry point turns them ON. Never --no-verify, never a forced main, never prints a token.
ship.py.purpose: REG-3646 - the one entry point for shipping a version: python3 tv/ship.py vNNNN runs the box rehearsal, ci/ push, Mac readiness, CI wait beside the Mac hook, failed-job makeup, and post-land checks.

shard_watch.py.gotcha: A real test failure is never auto-rerun; a cut-off, timeout, or infra kill is. GitHub refuses a mid-run rerun, so that case is queued for suite_makeup. choose_shards only bumps n_min when a split flag is up.
shard_watch.py.purpose: REG-3647..3652 - live per-job watch of agent / Playwright shards, pre-push rehearsal of a recently-failed shard set, 2-of-3 / near-ceiling split flags, and required-check judgement that ignores proof-keys windows jobs.

ship_yield.py.gotcha: UNKNOWN (GitHub unread) refuses a dry/ or grok/ push and never cancels a run. ci/ ship refs, main, and Publish itself are never cancelled or held. ci/*dry* names are always refused. Leftover proof-keys windows on a real ship branch do not keep the ship live (REG-3652).
ship_yield.py.purpose: REG-3653/3654 - while a real ship (ci/claude-* or ci/proof-keys-*) or a Publish run on main is live, or in the window after a main push until Publish finishes, dry/ and grok/ CI pushes yield the runners so a ship's or Publish's jobs never wait on our own test jobs. A sweeper cancels stale dry runs and any ci/*dry* name (never used again).
